doc.title: John Lamb interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 16, 2001

title: Teaching subjects and the John Lamb Trio
summary: He taught music, math and more, directed choir and band, and led a trio at a resort for a year.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: I was teaching music and math.

And social studies. Then while I was in this math thing I became re-certified. I went to the JC and picked up what, 16 credits, and immediately after that was done they took me out of math and put me back into music. So I became a choral director, and a band director. And then I decided that that was the end of it. But during all of this time I had continued to play on weekends and nights. And one year they had a jazz policy, where I worked six nights a week. All the jazz artists came in, oh guys that were on the road. For one year, it was at Tierverdi Island Resort I believe it’s called. We played there for all the greats, with a trio. It was called the John Lamb Trio and we went to do revues every week and we had a great time with that.
Wow. You’ve had an amazing life.
